fixed: A calendar file built to be slow no longer freezes the app for minutes on each import, or at each start with Import calendar when the app starts on: a repeating event set to repeat a number of times from a start far back is counted without walking every day since (one so far back that even that would take too long is listed under Repeating events the app can't read), a start in year 0000 is not read, a file with old Mac line ends is read as fast as any other, and many events sharing one identifier are offered once.
A long-lived calendar written oldest first no longer loses its upcoming gigs to the 5,000-event limit: events already over don't count toward it.
A calendar that arrives cut off part-way, as a dropped connection can leave it, no longer labels the programs whose events were in the lost part No longer in your calendar.

A moved or deleted date of a repeating event, or its end date, written in another form than the event's start (in UTC against a time zone, as some calendar programs do) is now read: the moved date is no longer offered twice, the deleted one is no longer offered, and an all-day series no longer loses its last day west of Greenwich.

Undo after importing from your calendar now moves the drafts you haven't touched to Recently deleted, as Undo at startup does, and keeps any you have started filling in. Before, it erased them, so an import at the next start added them again, and it erased a draft you had already edited.

The import's review now says when it shows a time your calendar keeps in UTC in this device's time zone, and the user guide says that an event imported while you are in another time zone keeps that zone's time.

changed: ICalRecurrence.datesThrough lists only from its from date, tries only the days the rule can fall on, takes maxTries and returns null past it, and reports the tries spent counting a COUNT series' earlier occurrences. planCalendarImport bounds them by iCalCountWorkLimit per feed, offers only the first series of a UID, matches RECURRENCE-ID and EXDATE values written in another form than DTSTART by local date and time, and reads an all-day series' UNTIL on its written date.

parseICalFeed takes today and does not count one-off events already over toward maxEvents; ICalFeed.complete says whether the document closed, and canJudgeMissing requires it. ICalDateValue.tryParse refuses year 0000. Unfolding is linear in the line's length.
